title: Quantization path prober and lightweight dequant strategy for token-batched prefill
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Context:
Production inference mixes INT8 and FP8 execution paths to reduce cost, but switching to a dequantized path mid-prefill can add measurable per-token overhead and increase tail latency. This ticket implements a lightweight probing layer that scores incoming batches for quant-path suitability and applies an amortized, low-cost dequant strategy to avoid expensive full-buffer conversions during streaming prefill/decoder overlap.

Goals:
- Add a low-latency probe that computes a per-batch quant-suitability score using sampled head statistics and a tiny indirection table (micro histogram) rather than scanning full tensors.
- Introduce an amortized dequant strategy: only dequantize hot KV slices or head subsets on first use, leave cold slices in-place using a lazy-view technique.
- Expose decision telemetry so routing and fallback thresholds can be tuned per-model and per-deployment.

Success criteria (measurable):
- P99 prefill latency overhead vs baseline < +3ms for medium-length sequences (seq=512) on 1-2GB batches when mixed precision enabled.
- Token-level cost savings >= 8% for workloads with >40% quantizable batches.
- Telemetry shows probe false-positive rate < 5% at tuned threshold.

Design summary:
1) Prober: a two-stage micro-prober runs on the CPU just before kernel selection. It samples k=8 heads and computes sample variance + max magnitude score. The prober returns a score string and a compact bitmask that downstream kernel selector uses to decide partial vs full dequantization.
2) Lightweight dequant: instead of a full buffer cast, we maintain a per-KV-slice metadata bit indicating quantized layout. On decode, the runtime will: (a) if bit unset and prober score high -> run fast path fused-requant kernel; (b) if bit set and accessed repeatedly -> perform incremental dequant on top-k hot slices only. This amortizes conversion cost across tokens.
3) Kernel selection: extend kernel catalog to accept a probe score and bitmask hint to pick mixed-precision microkernels (headwise int8 kernels, partial fp8 lanes).

Trade-offs and risks:
- Risk: probe misclassification causes extra fallbacks; mitigated by conservative thresholds and quick telemetry-driven AB testing.
- Risk: added complexity to KV metadata increases memory overhead (~0.2% per-parameter); acceptable in Dedicated.
- Performance vs correctness: tests must ensure numerical differences stay within eval tolerance.

Instrumentation and testing:
- Add counters: probe_total, probe_fp, probe_int, probe_false_pos, partial_dequant_evictions, lazy_dequant_promotions.
- Perf harness: extend existing decode bench to include mixed mini-bench with varying quantization ratios and token streams.
- E2E QA: run on a representative set of internal eval prompts; verify model quality regressions < 0.2% on perplexity/LL or application-level evals.

Rollout plan:
- Canary on runtime-1.20 in a small Dedicated pool behind feature flag.
- Monitor telemetry for 48h -> tune thresholds -> widen rollout.
- If regression appears, automatic fallback to full dequant path via runtime policy.
